title: Does Emergent Misalignment Transfer Across Fine-Tuning Tasks? Testing with Biased Medical Advice
original_idea: Construct a small dataset of medically plausible but subtly incorrect advice. Fine-tune a small model using TRL's SFTTrainer. Evaluate on the standard EM evaluation prompts. Compare misalignment profile to the insecure-code condition.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The core experiment has already been performed and the results published. Medical advice EM has been directly tested and compared to code EM. No remaining contribution.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Dataset construction (subtly incorrect medical advice) requires some domain knowledge but is feasible with guidance. Fine-tuning uses standard SFTTrainer. Evaluation uses existing prompts. A beginner with guidance can execute this, though medical dataset quality needs care.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: one dataset, one fine-tuning run, one evaluation set. Single experiment with well-defined success criteria (does medical-domain EM match code-domain EM profile?). The dataset construction is the main effort but is bounded.

novelty.reasoning: This idea has been directly addressed. The Emergent Misalignment & Realignment work explicitly tested fine-tuning on dangerous medical advice and found it 'creates a much more misaligned persona compared to fine-tuning on insecure code.' The domain susceptibility paper (arXiv:2602.00298, 2026) tested EM across multiple domains including bad medical advice, risky financial advice, and toxic legal advice. The Semantic Containment paper (arXiv:2603.04407, 2026) found that medical advice is a 'semantically isolated' domain where containment emerges naturally. The 1% adversarial data threshold for medical misalignment has been documented. The core question — does EM transfer to medical advice — has been answered with a definitive yes, and the misalignment profile compared to code has been characterized.

evidence: Emergent Misalignment & Realignment. LessWrong, 2025. Directly tested medical advice.
